events.title: Murad II dies, and Mehmed II takes the Ottoman throne for good
events.description: The death of Sultan Murad II brought his 18-year-old son Mehmed II back to power. Two years later Mehmed captured Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire.
events.html: The death of Sultan Murad II brought his 18-year-old son Mehmed II back to power. Two years later Mehmed captured Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Bartolomeu Dias lands at Mossel Bay after rounding the Cape
events.description: Having been driven round the southern tip of Africa by storms, Dias landed on the South African coast east of the Cape. His voyage showed that ships could sail from the Atlantic into the Indian Ocean.
events.html: Having been driven round the southern tip of Africa by storms, Dias landed on the South African coast east of the Cape. His voyage showed that ships could sail from the Atlantic into the Indian Ocean.

events.title: Dutch tulip prices collapse
events.description: At a bulb auction in Haarlem, buyers failed to appear and prices for tulip contracts crashed. 'Tulip mania' is often cited as the first recorded speculative bubble, though its damage is now thought modest.
events.html: At a bulb auction in Haarlem, buyers failed to appear and prices for tulip contracts crashed. 'Tulip mania' is often cited as the first recorded speculative bubble, though its damage is now thought modest.

events.title: Massachusetts Bay Colony issues paper money
events.description: To pay soldiers back from a failed expedition against Quebec, Massachusetts issued bills of credit, the first government paper money in the Americas (dated 1690 under the Old Style calendar).
events.html: To pay soldiers back from a failed expedition against Quebec, Massachusetts issued bills of credit, the first government paper money in the Americas (dated 1690 under the Old Style calendar).

events.title: London Protocol recognises an independent Greece
events.description: Britain, France and Russia agreed that Greece should be a fully independent kingdom, after nearly a decade of revolution against the Ottomans. It was the first new state to emerge in the Balkans.
events.html: Britain, France and Russia agreed that Greece should be a fully independent kingdom, after nearly a decade of revolution against the Ottomans. It was the first new state to emerge in the Balkans.

events.title: Fifteenth Amendment ratified, barring racial bars to voting
events.description: The amendment forbade denying citizens the vote on grounds of race, colour or previous servitude. Southern states later evaded it with poll taxes, literacy tests and intimidation for almost a century.
events.html: The amendment forbade denying citizens the vote on grounds of race, colour or previous servitude. Southern states later evaded it with poll taxes, literacy tests and intimidation for almost a century.

events.title: Sixteenth Amendment allows a US federal income tax
events.description: Ratification of the Sixteenth Amendment gave Congress power to tax incomes without dividing the tax among states by population. Income tax became the main source of federal revenue.
events.html: Ratification of the Sixteenth Amendment gave Congress power to tax incomes without dividing the tax among states by population. Income tax became the main source of federal revenue.

events.title: Battle of Manila begins
events.description: American and Filipino forces entered Manila to retake it from the Japanese. The month-long battle destroyed much of the city, and around 100,000 Filipino civilians died, many in Japanese massacres.
events.html: American and Filipino forces entered Manila to retake it from the Japanese. The month-long battle destroyed much of the city, and around 100,000 Filipino civilians died, many in Japanese massacres.

events.title: Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens and the Big Bopper die in a plane crash
events.description: Their light aircraft crashed in snow near Clear Lake, Iowa, shortly after take-off, killing all aboard. Don McLean later called it 'the day the music died' in his song 'American Pie'.
events.html: Their light aircraft crashed in snow near Clear Lake, Iowa, shortly after take-off, killing all aboard. Don McLean later called it 'the day the music died' in his song 'American Pie'.
